items.title: Jasper Taylor Interview, 1959-06-30
items.q: I believe Zutty could feel the beat.

ctx.x: He always seemed so happy. Always had that smile on his face.

And everything was his own. It came out of his own head. I don't think he patterned after anyone. And I used to tell him I'm going to have a lot of fun with him, and I told him I was going to make a musical bed spring. He said, well let me see it. And there was, Baby Hall was a famous five-stroke old man. He did it perfect. He was a good timekeeper, and I think that his, he was another one who could feel the beat. I believe Zutty could feel the beat. He just got to feel it. I've seen a lot of great drummers who…
I'm sure you can. Baby admired you, I know, a lot. He told me that several times.

items.title: 68359_Zutty Singleton oral history interview
items.q: This other fine show on the Burlesque Wheel with Jasper Taylor was playing drums.

ctx.x: Yes, that's what he wanted to do.
We saw more than that. This other fine show on the Burlesque Wheel with Jasper Taylor was playing drums. Jasper Taylor was in Joe

Jordan's band. And they played 'Sweet Georgia Brown' for a cat to dance by the name of Lovie Taylor. Boy and did that cat dance. And that music was so perfect behind this cat's taps. He was a tap dancer but it was soft shoe. He didn't have no taps on his shoes.
